I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. I did not check them against the Q2 reference values you gave, because this project's CLAUDE.md says not to run checks or compare results with example or reference values.

```json
{"a_segment": "enterprise", "a_net": 327011091, "b_customers": 244, "c_category": "svc", "c_net": 345585619, "d_month": "2025-09", "e_email": "u176@ex.com", "f_repeat": 228, "g_avg": 689505, "h_growth": 15.3}
```

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 327,011,091원 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 244 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 345,585,619원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u176@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 228 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 689,505원 |
| h. September vs. August growth | 15.3% |

The data had some inconsistencies, so I made these choices:
- **Segment and category labels:** Some differ only in letter case or extra spaces (for example `Enterprise `, ` consumer`, `SMB`). I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** There are 300 customer rows but only 250 distinct emails, and duplicates sometimes have different segments. For b, f and e, I counted one customer per email. For a, I used the segment on the customer row linked to each order.
- **Period and status:** I counted orders with `ordered_at` from 2025-07-01 up to (not including) 2025-10-01, using the UTC timestamps as stored. Only orders with status `paid` are included.
- **Refunds:** I added up refund quantities per order and product. Each refunded unit is valued at the discounted unit price, rounded down to the won.
- **Average per order (g):** The denominator is every paid order in Q3.

If those choices are wrong, the answers will be off. Running the same script for Q2 and comparing with your reference values would confirm them: `python3 -I /tmp/q3.py shop.db 2025-04-01 2025-07-01`.
